title: Reusable seed wafer: peel micron DRAM films, skip new ingots
idea: Inverts 'every die consumes a slab of crucible-grown silicon': grow a 5-8 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer on a seed wafer, bond it to a cheap carrier (reclaimed or low-grade wafer), cleave at the porous layer, re-polish the seed and repeat 30-50 times. The DRAM array and periphery only need the top few microns of perfect crystal.
why: Cuts Cz ingot, high-purity quartz crucible and polysilicon demand per bit ~20-40x (attacks the Spruce Pine >80% chokepoint) plus ingot-growth energy.

title: Dirty bulk, clean skin: metallurgical silicon substrate under thick epi
idea: Inverts 'the whole wafer must be 11N electronic grade': use upgraded-metallurgical-grade (5-6N) seed-cast mono silicon as the substrate, add a buried phosphorus/aluminum gettering layer and a carbon-doped epitaxial diffusion barrier, then grow a 10 um high-purity epitaxial skin from silane where all devices live.
why: UMG silicon needs ~15-20 kWh/kg vs ~50-70 kWh/kg for Siemens polysilicon (~3x lower embodied energy per wafer) and can come from US/Norway metallurgical plants instead of concentrated polysilicon makers.

title: Wordline-last: aluminum replaces tungsten after all hot steps
idea: Inverts 'buried wordlines are formed early, so they must be refractory tungsten': form a sacrificial poly-Si/SiN buried wordline, finish capacitors and every >450 C anneal, then exhume the sacrificial line through a slot and refill it with high-pressure reflowed aluminum on a thin TiN barrier (replacement-metal-gate logic applied to the DRAM array).
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 from the wordline; Al in narrow trenches gives ~1.5-2x lower line resistance than W plus barrier, cutting wordline RC; aluminum is smelted in North America.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in every chuck
idea: Inverts 'helium is the only safe backside heat-transfer gas': feed electrostatic chucks in etch/CVD/implant with 5-20 Torr hydrogen (thermal conductivity higher than He) from an on-site electrolyzer, recirculated through a palladium-membrane loop with sub-LEL leak sensing; the backside gas never touches plasma.
why: Backside cooling is one of the largest fab helium uses; removes dependence on Qatar (~30%, offline since March 2026) for that load; H2 is made from water and power on site.

title: Zero-vent fab: noble gases treated as leased capital, not consumables
idea: Inverts 'process gases are bought, used once and vented': a fab-wide exhaust spine with cryogenic fractional distillation and membranes recovers He, Ne, Kr, Xe and NF3 from every tool exhaust before abatement, repurifies to 6N and returns them to gas cabinets; the gas vendor keeps ownership and bills only for grams lost.
why: Targets >85% recovery of helium and neon (Qatar, Ukraine/Russia chokepoints), turning a supply shock into a small make-up stream; the lease model aligns the vendor with recovery.

title: Rutile TiO2 on MoO2 electrodes: k~90 without hafnium or ruthenium
idea: Inverts 'DRAM high-k must be ZrO2/HfO2 stacks on TiN or Ru': oxidize a molybdenum liner into a rutile MoO2 bottom electrode that templates low-temperature (<450 C) rutile TiO2 (k 80-110), with an Al-doped interfacial layer to suppress leakage.
why: Hits the k~70 requirement of the capacitor charge wall with Ti and US-mined Mo instead of Hf/Zr/Ru; ~2x capacitance at the same aspect ratio, or AR dropped from ~70:1 to ~40:1, cutting etch time and fluorocarbon gas use.

title: Grow the holes: anodized alumina pores as capacitor molds
idea: Inverts 'deep capacitor holes must be plasma-etched': deposit thick aluminum over the array and anodize it; self-ordered hexagonal pores with aspect ratios above 100:1 (pitch set by anodization voltage, registration seeded by a shallow imprint) become the capacitor mold, lined with electrode and dielectric by ALD.
why: Removes the hardest high-AR fluorocarbon etch (C4F6/C4F8, fluorspar and PFAS supply chain) and its hardmask stack; room-temperature aqueous electrochemistry reaches the AR~115 needed for more charge.

title: Cleanroom-free fab: wafers ride sealed nitrogen tunnels between tools
idea: Inverts 'the whole fab must be an ISO-class cleanroom': wafers stay permanently inside sealed N2-purged carriers that dock to sealed tools through an overhead N2/vacuum tunnel network, so the building itself is ordinary ISO-8 air and HVAC moves ~10x less air.
why: Cleanroom HVAC and makeup air are ~30-50% of fab electricity and drive humidification water; lowers shell capital and build time, easing US siting.

title: Waterless cleans: supercritical CO2 replaces ultrapure-water rinses
idea: Inverts 'cleaning means water': run post-etch residue removal, particle cleans and resist strip in supercritical CO2 with small co-solvent doses (alcohols, amine chelators), recompressing and recycling the CO2; near-zero surface tension also stops 70:1 capacitor pillars from collapsing during drying.
why: Cuts ultrapure-water use across DRAM's 100+ wet steps by an estimated 40-60% and removes pillar-collapse yield loss; feedstock can be captured industrial CO2.

title: Fab that breathes with the grid: buffer WIP to follow cheap power
idea: Inverts 'a fab runs flat out 24/7': size work-in-progress buffers in front of the most energy-hungry steps (epitaxy, furnaces, CVD, abatement burners, chillers) so they run hard during curtailed solar/wind hours and idle at peaks, add chilled-water thermal storage, and schedule with a cycle-time vs $/MWh co-optimizer.
why: Shifting ~30% of fab load to curtailed power cuts electricity cost ~20-30% and makes renewable-rich US regions viable fab sites.

title: DRAM refurbishment line: harvest dies from retired servers into CXL pools
idea: Inverts 'working memory is made new': an automated line takes decommissioned DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs, retests every chip at speed, re-bins by retention and speed, and remounts them on CXL memory-expander cards whose controller remaps weak rows and bridges old DDR protocols to CXL.
why: Recovering even 20% of the millions of DIMMs hyperscalers retire yearly adds bits with zero wafers, helium, tungsten or water; cost per bit close to test cost.

title: Sell imperfect dies: fractional-capacity DRAM with OS bad-page maps
idea: Inverts 'every die must be perfect': ship dies with up to 10-30% failing rows or subarrays as non-power-of-two capacity parts, with a signed bad-page map in an on-module EEPROM that firmware or the CXL controller reads at boot and never allocates.
why: Raises usable bits per wafer by recovering scrapped or downbinned dies (HBM yield is down 20-30%); every recovered die saves its full share of quartz, helium, energy and water.

title: Panel DRAM: memory arrays built on Gen-6 display glass
idea: Inverts 'memory is built on round single-crystal wafers': use idle LCD/OLED panel lines (1.5x1.8 m glass) with seed-directed excimer-laser-crystallized large-grain silicon access devices and stacked MIM capacitors to build a slower bulk-capacity tier, with small CMOS periphery dies bonded at the panel edge.
why: Glass needs no Cz crystal or quartz crucible; one panel is ~30x a 300 mm wafer and display capacity is underused; target 3-5x lower capital per bit for a capacity tier.

title: Reject wafers reborn as passive interposers, bypassing ABF substrates
idea: Inverts 'HBM needs prime silicon interposers or organic ABF laminates': regrind test and yield-reject wafers into passive redistribution interposers with 2-3 copper layers patterned on mature i-line steppers, then hybrid-bond DRAM stacks and logic directly onto them.
why: Interposer silicon and single-supplier ABF film are CoWoS/HBM chokepoints; reclaimed wafers cost ~10% of prime and consume no new crucible quartz.

title: Chemical autarky: make fab chemistries on site from air, water and salt
idea: Inverts 'chemicals are purchased from concentrated suppliers': on-site electrolyzers make H2, O2 and ozone from water, chlor-alkali cells make HCl and Cl2 from salt, H2O2 comes from electrochemical oxygen reduction and NH3 from a small Haber-Bosch unit, all distilled to electronic grade at point of use.
why: Removes multi-week logistics and single-country dependencies for the highest-volume wet and gas chemicals; strengthens US manufacturability and resilience.

title: Urban-mined tungsten: carbide scrap to domestic WF6 loop
idea: Inverts 'tungsten comes from mines (China ~80%)': dedicate US cemented-carbide scrap recycling (zinc-process and oxidation routes) to APT and then WF6 for fabs, and feed fab chamber scrapings and spent targets back into the same loop under long-term offtake contracts.
why: A few hundred tonnes per year of domestic scrap can cover US fab WF6 demand, insulating DRAM from tungsten export controls and price shocks.

title: Light as memory: silica fiber recirculating delay loops
idea: Inverts 'memory stores data at rest in matter': store bits as optical pulses circulating in a ~10-20 m silica fiber or silicon-nitride spiral loop with semiconductor-optical-amplifier regeneration, giving 50-100 ns worst-case access to 0.1-1 Mbit per loop at 1-10 Tb/s with WDM, a modern mercury delay line.
why: Built from the most abundant material (silica), with no capacitor, no DRAM fab, no tungsten; serves streaming buffers such as packet queues and KV-cache rings.

title: DNA origami places capacitor sites without EUV
idea: Inverts 'arrays must be patterned by light': DNA origami tiles made by bacterial fermentation self-assemble onto coarse pre-patterned landing pads and carry metal-oxide nanoparticle hardmask dots at 10-15 nm pitch that define capacitor and contact positions; the DNA is burned off after pattern transfer.
why: Replaces several of DRAM's 5-7 EUV layers (single-supplier tool, tin plasma source) with biologically manufactured patterning; capital per patterned layer down ~10x.

title: Cold-crucible Czochralski: silicon melt levitated, no quartz contact
idea: Inverts 'silicon melt must sit in a high-purity quartz crucible': hold the melt in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible by induction, with a thin frozen silicon skull as the container, and pull the crystal from it; electromagnetic stirring sets interstitial oxygen.
why: Eliminates Spruce Pine HPQ crucibles (>80% share); lower oxygen also tightens the retention tail; the crucible becomes permanent capital, not a consumable.

title: Stranded-memory exchange: CXL fabric rents idle DRAM across racks
idea: Inverts 'memory belongs to one server': a row-scale CXL 3 memory fabric plus a spot-market scheduler leases the ~25-35% of installed DRAM that sits stranded to other servers by the minute, with prices that steer tenants.
why: Raises usable supply ~20-30% with no new wafers, offsetting the 4x price spike; materials per useful bit fall by the same factor.

title: Wastewater to ultrapure water with fab waste heat
idea: Inverts 'UPW starts from fresh water': feed the UPW plant from municipal treated wastewater, use the fab's 30-40 C chiller reject heat to drive membrane distillation ahead of RO/EDI polishing, and send reject brine to industrial users.
why: Eliminates freshwater withdrawal (a DRAM fab uses millions of gallons per day), opening drought-prone US sites and turning waste heat into a resource.

title: Multi-beam electron writing for DRAM's critical layers
idea: Inverts 'critical layers must be printed by EUV from one supplier': use ~100k-beam electron direct write with silicon field-emitter tip arrays and blanking apertures, dedicated to DRAM's highly repetitive cell layers where pattern data compresses to a small repeat unit.
why: Removes EUV (single supplier, tin source) and masks for 5-7 layers; array regularity makes throughput tractable; target ~3x lower capital per critical layer.

title: Chokepoint-aware process kit: element budgets as design rules
idea: Inverts 'choose materials for performance, then source them': annotate every process module with grams of W, Hf, Ru, He, PFAS, quartz and water per wafer plus a supplier-concentration (HHI) index, and run a flow optimizer that picks the recipe meeting electrical targets at minimum chokepoint exposure.
why: Makes scarce-resource intensity a first-class metric; expected 30-60% cut in chokepoint-weighted inputs per bit by surfacing substitutions (Al for W, Mo for Ru, H2 for He).

title: Silicon carbide access transistor: retention outlives the server
idea: Inverts 'the access transistor must be silicon': build 1T1C cells on 4H-SiC (3.26 eV gap, intrinsic carriers ~1e-9 cm^-3) so junction and subthreshold leakage drop by many orders of magnitude and a 5 fF node holds its level for years at 85 C; refresh circuits are deleted and lines run in idle US 150/200 mm SiC power fabs.
why: Zero refresh power (16-33% of idle power) and no refresh bandwidth loss; Si and C are abundant; adds US capacity from existing SiC fabs.

title: Nitrogen-cooled racks freeze leakage, switching refresh off
idea: Inverts 'memory runs at room temperature': immerse DRAM modules in liquid nitrogen from air-separation units (no helium), where junction and subthreshold leakage fall by >1e6 and retention stretches from 64 ms to hours or days; firmware disables refresh for working sets whose lifetime is below the cryogenic retention.
why: Zero refresh power and bandwidth, wire resistance falls ~5x; nitrogen is the most abundant gas and LN2 costs cents per liter.

title: Ephemeral memory: data dies before charge does, so never refresh
idea: Inverts 'stored data must outlive cell retention': a refresh-less DRAM tier holds only AI activations, gradients, KV blocks and packet buffers whose lifetime the compiler/runtime proves is below a guaranteed 10-50 ms retention, with hardware write-timestamps that fault any read past the deadline.
why: Zero refresh power in that tier; cells can use ~30:1 instead of 70:1 capacitors, roughly halving mold, fluorocarbon etch gas and ALD precursor per bit, and refresh counters vanish from the periphery.

title: Buckled silicon-carbide nanobeam holds the bit mechanically
idea: Inverts 'bits are electric charge': each cell is a doubly clamped amorphous-SiC nanobeam deposited with built-in compressive stress so it rests buckled up or down; electrostatic pull electrodes snap it over in ~1-10 ns and capacitive sensing reads its position, with nothing to leak.
why: Zero refresh and zero standby; only Si, C and N, no high-k, Hf, Ru or W; SiC fatigue resistance targets >1e15 cycles.

title: Nano-relay switch with vacuum capacitor: zero off-current cells
idea: Inverts 'the access device is a leaky transistor and the capacitor needs high-k': replace the access transistor with a ~50 nm electrostatic nano-relay whose open contact is a true vacuum gap (no subthreshold current) and store charge on a plain SiO2 or vacuum-gap capacitor in the same sealed cavity, so retention is set only by surface leakage (years).
why: Zero refresh power and no access-transistor leakage tail; eliminates hafnia/zirconia and Ru; contacts in TiN or conductive carbon.

title: Wurtzite AlBN ferroelectric cell: hafnium-free, nonvolatile DRAM
idea: Inverts 'ferroelectric memory needs hafnia or lead': sputter wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N from abundant Al and B in N2 as the cell capacitor's ferroelectric in a 1T1C array whose sense amps read polarization-switching charge (remanent polarization >100 uC/cm2, ~5x HZO).
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; the huge polarization lets a planar or shallow capacitor replace 70:1 pillars, cutting etch gas and mold; no Hf, Zr or Pb, and AlN is already a US-made MEMS material.

title: Sliding ferroelectric boron nitride bilayers: switch by gliding, not ions
idea: Inverts 'polarization switching means displacing ions, which fatigues': store the bit in the stacking order (AB vs BA) of a bilayer hexagonal boron nitride, flipped by a vertical field that slides the layers one bond length; sliding creates no vacancies, so endurance may be effectively unlimited.
why: Nonvolatile, zero refresh; atomically thin cell made of boron and nitrogen only, with no Hf, W or PFAS chemistry.

title: Proton shuttle in phosphosilicate glass: nanosecond nonvolatile resistor
idea: Inverts 'memory state is held by electrons': drive protons under strong short field pulses through a few-nm phosphorus-doped SiO2 electrolyte into and out of a MoO3 or TiO2 channel, changing its conductance 10-100x; the proton stays put without power.
why: Zero refresh; materials are Si, P, O, H and Mo/Ti (abundant, US-available), at BEOL temperatures so it can stack over logic.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode latch cells in plain silicon
idea: Inverts 'a DRAM bit needs a storage capacitor': pair two degenerately doped silicon tunnel diodes (negative differential resistance) with one access transistor so the storage node sits at one of two stable points held by the NDR valley current, a static cell with no refresh.
why: Zero refresh and no capacitor (no pillars, Hf/Zr, Ru or high-AR fluorocarbon etch); only silicon and dopants; standby set by a ~pA valley current target.

title: Gate-coupled thyristor: a self-latching pure-silicon bit
idea: Inverts 'a cell is passive and must be topped up from outside': a vertical PNPN thyristor with a gate-coupled base latches on or off by its own regenerative gain; a low-gain design holds 'on' cells at sub-pA holding current and 'off' cells draw nothing, so no refresh cycle exists.
why: Zero refresh power; no capacitor, no high-k, fewer metal layers; a pure-silicon 4-6F2 cell buildable in older US fabs.

title: Cobalt- and platinum-free MTJ using iron shape anisotropy
idea: Inverts 'perpendicular MRAM needs Co, Pt, Ir, Ru and Ta': make tall Fe-B pillar free layers whose perpendicular anisotropy comes from shape (height > diameter) on an Fe/MgO interface, and pin the reference layer with a thick iron-nitride (Fe16N2) hard magnet instead of a Co/Pt synthetic antiferromagnet.
why: Nonvolatile with effectively unlimited endurance, so zero refresh; removes platinum-group metals and DRC cobalt from MRAM stacks.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cell with back-gate lockout
idea: Inverts 'oxide-semiconductor cells need indium and gallium': a 2T gain cell of amorphous Zn-Sn-O whose write transistor has a back gate held at about -2 V in standby, pushing off-current toward 1e-23 A so retention exceeds the data's useful life (target >1 year at 85 C) and refresh is removed.
why: Zero refresh; no indium (China ~60%) or gallium (China ~98%); sputtered and stackable at <400 C over logic.

title: Via-ROM for frozen AI weights: nothing to refresh
idea: Inverts 'working memory must be rewritable': store fixed model weights as present/absent or size-coded (2-bit) vias in a dense crosspoint read-only array using two custom mask layers on a mature node; changing the model re-spins only the via mask, and only activations use DRAM.
why: Zero refresh power with no capacitor, high-k or tungsten pillars; frees 50-80% of inference DRAM/HBM at 2-4 bits per F2.

title: Silicon double-barrier quantum-well memory: UltraRAM without indium or antimony
idea: Inverts 'nonvolatile memory must be slow and high-voltage': gate a floating node through a Si/SiO2/Si/SiO2 double barrier (two 1-2 nm oxides around a ~2 nm silicon well) that only conducts when a ~2.5 V write aligns the well level (resonant tunneling) and is opaque otherwise, giving ns writes and years of retention.
why: Zero refresh; elastic resonant transport avoids the hot-carrier oxide wear that limits flash; only Si and O, unlike InAs/AlSb UltraRAM.

title: Thin-film iron flux rings: core memory reborn at nanoscale
idea: Inverts 'core memory is obsolete': pattern ~60 nm Fe-Si alloy nanorings that hold clockwise or counterclockwise flux-closure states, switch them by current through a central post, and read them by the voltage spike induced in a sense line on switching (destructive read with write-back), as ferrite cores did.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; magnetic switching does not wear; no tunnel barrier, MgO, Co, Pt or Ru, just Fe and Si.

title: Back-end oxide CMOS latches: static memory stacked over logic
idea: Inverts 'static memory must live in the silicon substrate': build cross-coupled latches from n-type amorphous ZnO and p-type SnO/Cu2O thin-film transistors in the metal stack at <350 C, several tiers high, with wide-gap leakage below 1e-18 A per device.
why: Zero refresh with standby ~1000x below silicon SRAM; abundant Zn, Sn and Cu; no substrate area or capacitor materials.

title: No-refresh DDR standard lets non-DRAM fabs supply main memory
idea: Inverts 'main memory is defined by the DRAM cell': publish a JEDEC-style NR-DDR/CXL interface with no refresh commands, fixed read/write windows and a nonvolatile-capable flag, so SiC, oxide, ferroelectric or magnetic dies from power, display and 200 mm fabs drop into existing sockets.
why: Zero refresh power by specification and new supply from underused US fabs without DRAM-specific capacitor tools; widens the supplier base beyond three companies.

title: MgB2 persistent-current loops cooled without helium
idea: Inverts 'superconducting memory needs liquid helium': store bits as persistent currents in MgB2 loops (Tc 39 K; magnesium and boron are abundant) switched by kinetic-inductance gates, cooled to ~20 K by neon- or hydrogen-cycle cryocoolers instead of helium.
why: Persistent currents never decay, so zero refresh and near-zero static power; sidesteps the helium chokepoint for cryogenic AI or quantum data centers.

title: Iron spin-crossover molecules as electrically switched bistable bits
idea: Inverts 'memory materials must be inorganic crystals made in vacuum tools': use iron(II) spin-crossover complexes (Fe, N, C, H) with room-temperature hysteresis, switched between high- and low-spin states by field-induced ligand distortion and read by their volume and conductance change in a crossbar.
why: Bistable without power, so zero refresh; synthesized in solution from abundant elements and printed, with no W, Hf or PFAS.

title: Bacterial magnetite crystals as uniform nonvolatile bit cells
idea: Inverts 'memory materials are deposited by vacuum tools': harvest monodisperse ~45 nm magnetite crystals grown by magnetotactic bacteria in water at room temperature, self-assemble them onto chemically patterned sites as magnetic bits, and write and read them with crossed current lines and a Hall-sensor stripe.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; fermentation and iron replace sputtered Co/Pt stacks, and biological size uniformity removes the bit-to-bit spread that limits magnetic memory.

title: Abundant-elements-only zero-refresh memory prize
idea: Inverts 'industry picks materials, then finds supply': a federal staged prize ($50M/$250M/$1B) for a memory cell with >=10-year retention, >=1e15 endurance, <=50 ns access and DRAM-level cost per bit, built only from a whitelist of US-sourceable elements (no He, W, Hf, Ga, In, PGMs or PFAS) and judged on wafer-level arrays.
why: Pulls many teams toward chokepoint-free, zero-refresh cells while paying only for results; seeds a domestic manufacturing base.

title: Token-loop restoration: inference reads restore weights before they fade
idea: Inverts 'refresh must be a separate maintenance operation': lay out inference weights so every row is activated (and thus restored by its sense amplifier) once per decoding step (<20 ms) and remove refresh from those banks; if the token loop stalls, the read-only weights are dropped and re-streamed from flash.
why: Zero refresh power and ~10% bandwidth back in weight banks; the 20 ms retention target allows shorter capacitors with less mold and fluorocarbon etch per bit.

title: Vacuum-gap floating gate: flash physics without oxide wear
idea: Inverts 'a floating gate needs an oxide tunnel barrier, which wears out': suspend the floating node over a sealed 2-3 nm vacuum gap and charge it by Fowler-Nordheim field emission across vacuum with ~8 V local pulses; vacuum holds no traps to damage, so endurance is effectively unlimited, and at read fields emission is nil, so retention lasts years.
why: Zero refresh, nonvolatile, unlimited-endurance cell from Si, SiO2 and TiN only, with no high-k or Hf.
